journey:nesterov-holy-rus.l: State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, Russia

x.summary: In a snowy northern landscape beside a small monastery, Christ, accompanied by Saints Nicholas, Sergius of Radonezh and George, comes out to meet a crowd of Russian pilgrims: monks, peasants, the sick and the sorrowing. The quiet, pale palette makes the encounter feel like a vision within ordinary life. Nesterov intended the painting as an image of the soul of Russian faith.
facts: Nesterov worked on the composition for several years, making many studies of pilgrims and of the landscape of the Russian north.

The painting provoked sharp debate when it was first exhibited in 1907: it won a gold medal at the Munich International Exhibition of 1909, while critics such as Maximilian Voloshin found its Christ theatrical and unconvincing.
Nesterov also painted murals for the Vladimir Cathedral in Kyiv and the Marfo-Mariinsky Convent in Moscow.
